response.justification: Strong, versatile engineer with genuine geospatial credibility (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and some low-latency systems work (D at Sociomantic handling millions of req/s with async I/O, fibers, caching). However, the role's primary requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial/open-source settings — is only weakly evidenced: roughly seven months of C/C++ at National Instruments over a decade ago plus a university thesis project, with no Rust at all. Recent years are predominantly TypeScript/Node full-stack and AI tooling. There is also no navigation guidance, routing engine, or map-tile pipeline experience. Worth a screening call only if the team values systems-adjacent D experience and geospatial domain knowledge enough to accept a significant C++ ramp-up; otherwise this is a mismatch on the core technical bar.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS domain experience, including a founded open-source geo-data platform
Low-latency, high-throughput distributed services experience (async I/O, fibers, caching in D)
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, testing tooling authorship, mentoring and public talks
concerns: Modern C++ experience is minimal and ~10 years stale; no Rust experience
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline work; GIS work is web/app-level, not data pipeline
Recent career trajectory is full-stack TypeScript/Node, not systems-level backend
